name: Dopamine
executiveSummary: Dose-dependent catecholamine. Usual ranges: **2–5 mcg/kg/min** (dopaminergic), **5–10 mcg/kg/min** (inotropic), **10–20 mcg/kg/min** (vasopressor). Pediatrics/NICU: **2–20 mcg/kg/min** (common max **50 mcg/kg/min**). Central line + pump.
indications:
## Indications

- Shock with low output / hypotension when inotropy ± vasoconstriction is desired.
- Historical “renal” low-dose use: limited evidence vs norepinephrine in sepsis.

## Precautions

- Tachycardia, arrhythmias, peripheral vasoconstriction at high doses; extravasation → necrosis.
- Incompatible with alkaline solutions (bicarbonate).

> Titrate to MAP/perfusion; prefer central line.

adulto.presentation: Ampule 40 mg/mL (5 mL) or institutional vial.
adulto.finalConcentration: E.g. **800 mcg/mL** (200 mg in 250 mL) or **1600 mcg/mL** (fluid restriction) — local guide.
adulto.dose: **2–20 mcg/kg/min** continuous IV; titrate. Orient.: **2–5** dopaminergic; **5–10** inotropic; **10–20** vasopressor. Common max **20–50 mcg/kg/min** ICU only.
adulto.notes: Monitor HR, BP, urine output, and infusion site.

pediatrico.finalConcentration: Usual **3.2 mg/mL**; up to **6 mg/mL** if fluid restriction.
pediatrico.dose: **2–20 mcg/kg/min** continuous IV; usual max **50 mcg/kg/min**.
pediatrico.notes: Antagonized by beta-blockers; high-dose vasoconstriction by alpha-blockers. Discard if abnormal color.

neonatal.dose: **2–10 mcg/kg/min** continuous IV (up to **20 mcg/kg/min** if refractory) — neonatology.

stability:
## Stability

- Pump dilution: ~24 h room temperature (local guide). Protect from light. Discard if oxidized.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Tachycardia, arrhythmias, hypertension/hypotension, nausea, vasoconstriction, necrosis from extravasation.

bibliography.citation: Surviving Sepsis — norepinephrine preferred over dopamine in most septic shock.
